correctness.rationale: The proof reduces total domination in a bipartite graph to two shore-cover numbers, proves a sharp pair-cover lemma by induction, converts every sub-target total-bondage candidate into that lemma, and supplies a matching construction. Direct computation from the definitions exhausts all sub-target deletion sets for orders \(n=3,4,5\), independently obtains pair-cover minima \(3,5,7,9\) for \(n=3,4,5,6\), and checks the construction through \(n=30\). The computation is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are the canonical perfect-matching deletion of complete bipartite graphs, a standard exact-value family in total-bondage theory. The theorem gives a full infinite-family classification and a structural pair-cover explanation for the sharp change from the known balanced baseline \(b_t(K_{n,n})=n\) to \(2n-3\). This is not a routine single-instance computation.
